01 /

Problem

SayRight is designed for Chinese-speaking users who need English for practical communication, particularly at work and in everyday situations. It connects help with an immediate expression to the option of practising that expression later.

The intended audience is a product focus, not a market-validated user profile. Learning gains have not been established.

02 /

Product Vision

Use now → Save if valuable → Practise later.

Correct starts from an English draft; Express starts from a Chinese intention. Both can lead into the same personal expression collection and review system. Saving remains an explicit choice: immediate help should not depend on completing a lesson.

03 /

My Role

As an Independent Software & Product Developer, I work across product design, requirements, engineering collaboration, problem solving and test acceptance. Project records document my acceptance of the practice-suggestion and context-practice features, alongside manual review of the offline semantic-evidence workflow.

Development uses AI coding tools; this case study does not claim sole authorship of the implementation.

04 /

Key Features

01

Correct and Express

Get language assistance from an English draft or a Chinese intention, then choose whether an expression is worth keeping.

02

Saved expressions, recall and review

Save explicitly, reuse an existing asset or keep a separate one, and return for active recall. Saving and completing a recall exercise are distinct events.

03

Practice grounded in context

Suggestions draw on eligible completed learning records. Context practice invites a new English attempt before requesting help; it does not automatically save, score or record learning progress.

05 /

Technical Approach

Electron brings together a JavaScript, HTML and CSS interface with a local SQLite database. Main owns business services, database transactions, provider execution and credentials; preload exposes narrow interfaces to the Renderer.

SQLite uses WAL, foreign-key enforcement and explicit transactions. Saved expressions, source information, review state and completed learning events have separate roles. Model requests pass through registered provider/model profiles and fixed adapters, with deadlines, bounded response reading, cancellation and validation. Credential storage uses Electron encryption interfaces.

06 /

Engineering Challenges

Keeping request lifetime separate from feedback

A Settings defect cleared the interface’s operation lock while Main still held a pending connection test. A second action was rejected but surfaced as a misleading input error. The fix retained request ownership until Main completed and suppressed obsolete feedback.

Historical record, October 2026: 55 focused synthetic checks passed. These cover the identified race. An earlier reported connection error remains unexplained.

Locating evidence without trusting model arithmetic

A live research response arrived successfully but failed validation: its quotation and UTF-16 offsets disagreed. Subsequent work moved position calculation into a bounded local locator, rejecting missing or ambiguous quotations and invalid text boundaries. The original failure remained a failure.

Exact location does not prove semantic correctness. This research remains gated from ordinary live product use.

07 /

Testing & Iteration

Testing separates software behaviour from model quality. Historical records distinguish offline tests, actual Electron integration, cloud-runner checks, local manual review and limited real-provider experiments.

Selected historical records · October 2026
ScopeRecorded result and boundary
Semantic core121 Node checks passed, 5 skipped; 126 Electron checks passed, none skipped. Synthetic contract checks, not real-model evaluation.
Practice workflowsElectron integration checks covered suggestions and context practice, including read-only database boundaries. Isolated synthetic data and controlled generation; no learning-effect claim.
Live semantic researchOne earlier response was rejected and the experiment stopped. A separate two-case experiment passed manual review by the project owner; this is too small to establish general reliability.

These are separate development records, not a combined test total or a fresh portfolio test run. Cloud-runner checks used a synthetic credential path and made no provider calls. Live results do not automatically qualify later prompts.

08 /

Current Development Status

As of 28 October 2026, the audited package identifies itself as 3.3.0, with further work on the v3.4 development branch. SayRight remains in development, with public-release checks still outstanding.

  • Implemented: expression assistance, saved assets, recall/review, practice suggestions and context practice.
  • Partially validated: semantic-evidence work has offline synthetic checks and manual review by the project owner; native interaction checks remain partial.
  • Pending: real-model validation of the current semantic-evidence implementation, remaining accessibility checks and public-release gates. Learning effectiveness is unverified.

Public Demo on GitHub — a separate demonstration repository, not the complete SayRight product source.
